metaDescription: Flat-pack furniture assembly for LA homes and apartments. Fixed pricing, $135–$295. See what's included and when to hire a pro.
intro: That flat-pack wardrobe or new sectional isn't going to build itself, and in Los Angeles the mix of tight apartment elevators, narrow bungalow hallways, and multi-box furniture shipments means assembly often takes longer than the instructions suggest. Whether you're in a new-build apartment downtown or a pre-war bungalow in Highland Park, getting furniture assembled correctly the first time saves you from wobbly shelves or stripped screws later.
causes: Furniture kits often ship with unclear or translated instructions that skip steps.
Pre-drilled holes don't always align because panels shift slightly during shipping.
Many people don't own the right tools, like a power driver with adjustable torque, leading to stripped screws.
Multi-person items like bed frames or large wardrobes are hard to hold steady and align solo.
Older pre-war bungalows sometimes have uneven floors that make leveling large pieces tricky.
whatProDoes: Unboxes and inventories all parts and hardware before starting, checking for shipping damage or missing pieces.
Reads the manufacturer's assembly sequence and follows torque and alignment steps to avoid stripped screws.
Assembles the piece using proper tools, including drivers and clamps for large or heavy panels.
Levels and stabilizes the finished piece, checking that drawers, doors, and shelves operate correctly.
Clears packaging materials and does a final check for loose screws or wobble.
diyOrPro: Simple items like a small bookshelf or side table are reasonable to assemble yourself if you're comfortable with basic tools and have an hour to spare. Larger or multi-box furniture, like wardrobes, bed frames, or modular sectionals, is harder to align solo and easier to damage or misassemble, especially in tight LA apartment layouts. If a piece requires wall anchoring for stability (like a tall bookcase or dresser), that step matters for safety and is worth having done correctly.
priceNote: This job runs $135 to $295 in Los Angeles, based on an $87/hour rate for a typical 1-3 hour job. The time it takes depends on the number of pieces, the complexity of the furniture, and how much space a pro has to work in, which varies a lot between a spacious new-build apartment and a cramped bungalow room.

faqs.q: Do I need to have the furniture already unboxed?
faqs.a: No, the pro will unbox everything and check the parts against the instructions as part of the job.

faqs.q: Can one pro assemble a large piece like a bed frame or wardrobe alone?
faqs.a: Most single items can be handled by one person, but very large or heavy pieces may take longer within the 1-3 hour range to account for maneuvering and alignment.

faqs.q: Will the pro mount furniture to the wall for tip-over safety?
faqs.a: Basic wall anchoring for stability can often be included, but let the pro know in advance since it may require additional hardware or time.
